title: Sport Pilot Airplane
note: Questions and choices are reproduced from the FAA sample-question document (a U.S. Government work). The FAA document has no answer key: answers and explanations are written by OpenChecklists and cite FAA sources.

questions.stem: With respect to the certification of airmen, which is a category of aircraft?

choices.C: Single-engine land and sea, multiengine land and sea.

questions.explanation: For airman certification, the categories of aircraft are airplane, rotorcraft, glider and lighter-than-air (plus powered-lift, powered parachute and weight-shift-control). Gyroplane and helicopter are classes of rotorcraft, and single-/multiengine land/sea are classes of airplane.

questions.stem: Which aircraft has the right-of-way over all other air traffic?

choices.C: An aircraft on final approach to land.

questions.explanation: An aircraft in distress has the right-of-way over all other air traffic.

questions.stem: May a pilot operate an aircraft that is not in compliance with an Airworthiness Directive (AD)?

choices.B: Yes, if allowed by the AD.

questions.explanation: Operating a product that does not meet an applicable AD is a violation, unless the AD itself allows the operation, for example through a compliance time or a special flight permit to reach a repair facility.

questions.stem: Which is true with respect to formation flights? Formation flights are

choices.A: authorized when carrying passengers for hire, with prior arrangement with the pilot in command of each aircraft in the formation.
choices.B: not authorized, except by arrangement with the pilot in command of each aircraft.
choices.C: not authorized, unless the pilot in command of each aircraft is trained and found competent in formation.

questions.explanation: No one may fly in formation except by arrangement with the pilot in command of each aircraft, and formation flight is never allowed while carrying passengers for hire.

questions.stem: How long does the Airworthiness Certificate of an aircraft remain valid?

choices.A: As long as the aircraft has a current Registration Certificate.
choices.B: Indefinitely, unless the aircraft suffers major damage.
choices.C: As long as the aircraft is maintained and operated as required by Federal Aviation Regulations.

questions.explanation: A standard airworthiness certificate stays in effect as long as maintenance, preventive maintenance and alterations are performed in accordance with parts 43 and 91 and the aircraft is registered in the United States.

questions.stem: A pilot can expect a wind-shear zone in a temperature inversion whenever the windspeed at 2,000 to 4,000 feet above the surface is at least
questions.explanation: Low-level wind shear is commonly associated with temperature inversions when the winds just above the inversion are strong. The usual rule of thumb is 25 knots or more at 2,000 to 4,000 feet.

questions.explanation: 18004KT in the KJFK report means wind from 180° at 4 knots. Wind direction in METARs is referenced to true north.

questions.stem: What is ground effect?

choices.A: The result of the interference of the surface of the Earth with the airflow patterns about an aircraft.
choices.B: The result of an alteration in airflow patterns increasing induced drag about the wings of an aircraft.
choices.C: The result of the disruption of the airflow patterns about the wings of an aircraft to the point where the wings will no longer support the aircraft in flight.

questions.explanation: Ground effect is the interference of the surface with the airflow around a wing within about one wingspan of the ground. It reduces upwash, downwash and wingtip vortices, and with them induced drag.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 5-11, Aerodynamics of Flight

questions.stem: An aircraft leaving ground effect during takeoff will

choices.A: experience a reduction in ground friction and require a slight power reduction.
choices.B: experience an increase in induced drag and a decrease in performance.
choices.C: require a lower angle of attack to maintain the same lift coefficient.

questions.explanation: Climbing out of ground effect, the wing needs a higher angle of attack for the same lift, and induced drag increases. Performance drops, and an airplane lifted off too slowly may settle back.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 5-11, Aerodynamics of Flight

questions.stem: What is the antidote when a pilot has the hazardous attitude of `Invulnerability`?

choices.C: It will not happen to me.

questions.explanation: The antidote for invulnerability ("It won't happen to me") is "It could happen to me."

questions.stem: What is the relationship of lift, drag, thrust, and weight when the airplane is in straight-and-level flight?

choices.A: Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag.
choices.B: Lift, drag, and weight equal thrust.
choices.C: Lift and weight equal thrust and drag.

questions.explanation: In straight-and-level, unaccelerated flight the forces are in equilibrium: lift equals weight and thrust equals drag.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 5-1, Aerodynamics of Flight

questions.stem: Name the four fundamentals involved in maneuvering an aircraft.

choices.C: Straight-and-level flight, turns, climbs, and descents.

questions.explanation: Every flight is built from four fundamentals: straight-and-level flight, turns, climbs and descents.

cites.label: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C), ch. 3, Basic Flight Maneuvers

questions.stem: Given the following: True course: 050 True heading: 040 True airspeed: 75 kts Groundspeed: 65 kts Determine the wind direction and speed.
questions.explanation: The 10° left wind correction means the wind is from the left, and groundspeed is 10 knots below TAS, so there is a headwind component. Solving the wind triangle (75 kt at 040° through the air, 65 kt at 050° over the ground) gives wind from about 355° at about 16 knots.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 21.) What is the estimated time en route from Mercer County Regional Airport (area 3) to Minot International (area 1)? The wind is from 330° at 25 knots and the true airspeed is 100 knots. Add 3-1/2 minutes for departure and climb-out.
questions.explanation: Mercer County to Minot measures about 59 NM on a true course of about 010°. With wind from 330° at 25 knots and 100 knots TAS, the wind correction angle is about 9° left and groundspeed about 80 knots: roughly 44.5 minutes en route plus 3.5 minutes for departure, about 48 minutes.

questions.explanation: Lakeview (30F) lies in the Class B sector labeled 110/30: ceiling 11,000 feet MSL, floor 3,000 feet MSL.

questions.stem: The most effective method of scanning for other aircraft for collision avoidance during daylight hours is to use

choices.A: regularly spaced concentration on the 3-, 9-, and 12-o`clock positions.
choices.B: a series of short, regularly spaced eye movements to search each 10-degree sector.
choices.C: peripheral vision by scanning small sectors and utilizing off-center viewing.

questions.explanation: Daytime scanning should use short, regularly spaced eye movements that bring successive 10° sectors into central vision, viewing each for at least 1 second. Peripheral, off-center viewing is a night technique.

questions.stem: An ATC clearance means an authorization by ATC for an aircraft to proceed under specified conditions within
questions.explanation: 14 CFR 1.1 defines an ATC clearance as an authorization by ATC to proceed under specified traffic conditions within controlled airspace, to prevent collisions between known aircraft.

questions.stem: When a distress or urgency condition is encountered, the pilot of an aircraft with a coded radar beacon transponder, who desires to alert a ground radar facility, should squawk code
questions.explanation: Squawk 7700 in a distress or urgency condition to alert ATC radar facilities.

questions.stem: Inbound to an airport with no tower or UNICOM in operation, a pilot should self- announce on MULTICOM frequency
questions.explanation: At airports without a tower or UNICOM, self-announce on MULTICOM (122.9) about 10 miles out, then on downwind, base, final and when leaving the runway.

questions.stem: An ATC radar facility issues the following advisory to a pilot flying on a heading of 270°: `TRAFFIC 3 O`CLOCK, 2 MILES, EASTBOUND...` Where should the pilot look for this traffic? ​
questions.explanation: Clock positions are relative to the nose. On a heading of 270°, 3 o'clock is 90° to the right, which is north.

questions.stem: The direct cause of every stall is excessive
questions.explanation: A wing stalls when it exceeds its critical angle of attack, regardless of airspeed, flight attitude or weight.

questions.stem: The best speed to use for a glide is one that will result in the greatest glide distance for a given amount of
questions.explanation: Best glide speed gives the greatest gliding distance for the altitude lost, at the best lift-to-drag ratio.

questions.explanation: The obstacle southeast of Winnsboro is charted at 903 feet MSL (323 AGL). Clearing it by 500 feet requires 903 + 500 = 1,403 feet MSL.

questions.explanation: Measure 19 minutes south of the 48° N line and 36 minutes west of the 101° W meridian to plot the position. It falls on Fischer (Pvt) airport.

questions.stem: Which combination of atmospheric conditions will reduce aircraft takeoff and climb performance?

choices.A: Low temperature, low relative humidity, and low density altitude.
choices.B: High temperature, low relative humidity, and low density altitude.
choices.C: High temperature, high relative humidity, and high density altitude.

questions.explanation: High temperature, high humidity and high density altitude all mean less dense air. The engine makes less power, the propeller produces less thrust and the wing needs more true airspeed, so takeoff and climb performance suffer.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 4-4, Principles of Flight

questions.stem: If the outside air temperature (OAT) at a given altitude is warmer than standard, the density altitude is
questions.explanation: Warmer-than-standard air is less dense, so density altitude is higher than pressure altitude.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 4-4, Principles of Flight

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 8.) Determine the pressure altitude at an airport that is 1,386 feet MSL with an altimeter setting of 29.97.
questions.explanation: Pressure altitude is field elevation plus the conversion factor for the altimeter setting. 29.97 lies between 29.92 (0) and 30.0 (-73), giving about -45 feet, so 1,386 - 45 ≈ 1,341 feet.

questions.stem: What does the red line on an airspeed indicator represent?
questions.explanation: The red radial line marks VNE, the never-exceed speed.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 8, Flight Instruments

questions.stem: Under what condition is indicated altitude the same as true altitude?

choices.A: If the altimeter has no mechanical error.
choices.B: When at sea level under standard conditions.
choices.C: When at 18,000 feet MSL with the altimeter set at 29.92.

questions.explanation: Indicated altitude equals true altitude only under standard atmospheric conditions with the altimeter correctly set, for example at sea level on a standard day. Nonstandard temperature or pressure makes them differ.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 8-4, Flight Instruments

questions.stem: A go-around from a poor landing approach should

choices.A: not be attempted unless circumstances make it absolutely necessary.
choices.B: generally be preferable to last minute attempts to prevent a bad landing.
choices.C: not be attempted after the landing flare has been initiated regardless of airspeed.

questions.explanation: An early decision to go around from a poor approach is generally preferable to last-minute attempts to salvage the landing.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 20, area 3.) What is the recommended communications procedure for departure at Currituck County Airport?

choices.A: Broadcast intentions prior to taxi and announcing runway of departure.
choices.B: Calling the Elizabeth City tower on 120.5.

questions.explanation: Currituck County is non-towered (CTAF 122.9). Self-announce your intentions before taxiing and announce the departure runway.
